newsitem.title: USA: Use of attention-deficit drug doubles - U.S. study.
newsitem.headline: Use of attention-deficit drug doubles - U.S. study.

text.p: Use of the drug Ritalin to treat children with attention deficit disorder has doubled in the United States in the past few years, a study said Tuesday.

Researchers in Maryland said the increase was due in part to longer courses of treatment, which now last into the teen years, to public acceptance of the drug as useful and to more girls using the medication.

The drug, known generically as methylphenidate, saw a 2 1/2-fold increase in use between 1990-1995, according to the report published in this month's issue of Pediatrics, the journal of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

The study, based on a search of several databases recording prescription drug use, was made by the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine, the Baltimore County Health Department and the University of Maryland at Baltimore.
By 1995, 1.5 million American children between the ages of 5 and 18 were taking the drug to control hyperactivity and improve performance in school and social settings, it said.
